Compare CH, unrestricted sandwich and both calibrated robustness values

sandwich_rv.Rd

Returns a practitioner table with RV_CH, RV_sand, RV_cal_delta and RV_cal_profile on the same partial-R-squared scale and test cutoff.

Usage

sandwich_rv(model, treatment, benchmarks = NULL, vcov = "HC1",
  cluster = NULL, k = 1, alpha = 0.05, critical = NULL, null = 0, ...)
# S3 method for class 'sandwich_rv_analysis'
print(x, ...)
# S3 method for class 'sandwich_rv_analysis'
summary(object, ...)
# S3 method for class 'sandwich_rv_analysis'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

model

Unweighted lm with an intercept and full-rank design.

treatment

One target model-matrix column.

benchmarks

Observed control units; NULL selects scalar terms.

vcov

HC0/HC1, one-way CR0/CR1, HAC_Bartlett_L4, HAC_QS_BW5, TWCR0_raw, TWCR1_raw, or a fixed covariance rule.

cluster

One- or two-way cluster labels aligned with fitted rows, or a formula.

k

Positive profile multiplier; default one.

alpha

Two-sided significance level.

critical

Optional fixed cutoff common to the comparison.

null

Null coefficient value.

...

Numerical solver arguments from rv_sand; unused in methods.

x,object

A sandwich_rv_analysis.

row.names,optional

Standard data-frame method arguments.

Details

The calibrated searches are run first so their independently verified indices can also improve the unrestricted upper bound, after rechecking. The two calibrated classes are not generally nested. A point estimate is shown only when bounds close within tolerance. The table's CH row uses the sandwich cutoff; the conventional default-cutoff reference is retained separately as RV_CH_standard.

Value

A sandwich_rv_analysis with table, three full results, benchmark diagnostics, RV_CH, RV_CH_standard, and k. summary() and as.data.frame() return the four-row table. Its benchmark column labels positive, zero and unavailable calibrations separately from computational status.

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + disp, data = mtcars)
sandwich_rv(fit, "wt", c("hp", "disp"), n_starts = 4,
            max_iterations = 20, search_steps = 3)
#> Robustness values for loss of significance (partial R-squared scale)
#>         measure estimate     lower     upper            status benchmark
#>           RV_CH 0.242656 0.2426556 0.2426556        ANALYTICAL      <NA>
#>         RV_sand       NA 0.0203211 0.0825404  CERTIFIED_BOUNDS      <NA>
#>    RV_cal_delta 0.269198 0.2691982 0.2691982 POINT_CERTIFICATE      zero
#>  RV_cal_profile 0.269198 0.2691982 0.2691982 POINT_CERTIFICATE      zero
#>  critical
#>   2.05183
#>   2.05183
#>   2.05183
#>   2.05183
#> Profile multiplier k = 1 
#> Bounds are computational intervals; see status for unavailable or unresolved values.
